title: Curcumin Market Size to Attain USD 123.64 Million in 2026
abstract:
The global curcumin market size reached at USD 110.59 million in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 123.64 million in 2026 to reach USD 337.39 million by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 11.8% from 2026 to 2035. The increased prevalence of several diseased conditions associated with cardiovascular, chronic, hepatocellular, and neurological disorders and the emerging need to prevent and treat them effectively drives the growth of the market.

Curcumin refers to a phenolic phytochemical extracted from the Curcuma longa rhizome that exhibits several biological activities and drug-like properties, being natural compounds. Due to this, it is ideally used to develop compounds and discover drugs for treating chronic illnesses. The curcumin market is experiencing significant growth due to the numerous pharmacological benefits of curcumin, including its antimutagenic, anti-inflammatory, [antioxidants](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/antioxidants-market), and antimicrobial properties. Moreover, curcumin provides immunoregulatory, chemo preventive, and chemotherapeutic properties.
According to the National Turmeric Board (NTB), India dominates the global turmeric industry by having major varieties with geographical indication tags, such as Erode Turmeric (Tamil Nadu), Kandhamal Haldi (Odisha), and Lakadong Turmeric (Meghalaya), that are known for high curcumin content. According to clinical trial studies conducted by the National Cancer Institute (NCI), the curcumin-containing products showcase anticancer and anti-oral mucositis effects in the paediatric population.  
The [biomarkers](https://www.towardshealthcare.com/insights/biomarkers-market-sizing) studies allow us to test the applications of curcumin-containing products as an adjunctive therapy. Research studies suggest a possible antitumor effect of curcumin-containing products. Patients with metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) can undergo research involving iMAtinib and curcumin-containing products. It is possible to explore the tolerability, efficacy, and feasibility of DOCEtaxel plus are the products that contains in the curcumin which helps in the treatment of cancer.  
The increased cost-effectiveness of certain antimicrobial medications and the increased prevalence of antimicrobial drug resistance are the emerging challenges in the curcumin market. According to researchers, this drug resistance can result in a global cause of death. There is an urgent need for improvements and modifications in natural antimicrobial agents to address these issues in chemically synthesized medicines.
The presence of prominent companies like BioMaxLifesciences Ltd. which is primarily located in India (Hyderabad, Telangana) upholds the regional market’s statistics. BioMaxLifesciences Ltd. introduced various products and services, including weight management medicines, antioxidant extracts, spray-dried vegetable powder, natural food colors, [nutraceuticals](https://www.towardsfnb.com/insights/insights/nutraceuticals-market), and oleoresins. BioMaxLifesciences Ltd. launched several nutraceuticals, such as lutein, lycopene, methyl sulphonyl methane, mono ammonium glycyrrginate, and Soy Isoflavone. Moreover, this company has also introduced natural food colors related to paprika, red beet root, and safflower yellow.

The Union Minister for Commerce and Industry announced the launch of the National Turmeric Board (NTB), which includes the representatives of the Ministry of AYUSH, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Department of Pharmaceuticals, and the Department of Commerce as prominent members. India accounts for 70% of global production and 62% of global trade for turmeric. India holds the first position as the largest producer, consumer, and exporter of turmeric. Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are the largest turmeric-producing states.
